question: what are voluntary rerouting scenarios
ground_truth: Voluntary rerouting 1. Your first guide with any rerouting request must be the ATC command. If an airline has the ATC functionality, it should also work with rerouting requests (Please note that for Sabre ATC after rerouting is not always guarantee). Note: In case of partially used tickets, the ATC is most likely not to correspond in rerouting scenarios. 2. If ATC is not an option, then as per usual you should consult the fare rules. First we check the ‘’PENALTIES’’ section of the fare rules to make sure that we can reschedule and that rerouting is allowed. After checking ‘’PENALTIES’’, open the ‘’RULE/ FLT APPLICATION’’ section of the fare rules so as to check the area/country/continent eligibility of the fare booked. Remember, most usually rerouting is not allowed from one area to another, neither to the departure airport nor to the arriving one. Additionally, changing the IATA area origin is forbidden. ATTENTION: Most airlines do not permit rerouting from domestic to international or regional flights, and vice versa, in accordance with IATA regulations. It is essential to review the airline's specific fare rules to identify any possible exceptions, as well as consult Edvin Documents for additional guidance. Partially used tickets: Please pay attention to partially used tickets and rerouting requests. Once part of the ticket has been used, then this part of the itinerary is binding to the rest of the ticket and any rerouting request is subject to the OB used itinerary. This means that the remaining coupons have to start and finish from the IATA sub area that they already are. Always check the ‘’Rules/FLT Application’’ section of the fare rules, to make sure of how restrictive the fare is. For example: Let’s say we have a RT ticket from the USA to Europe. Pax has already used the OB, e.g LAX-FRA and the IB FRA-LAX is left. Rerouting scenarios/ examples: MUC-LAX Possible LON-LAX Possible FRA-NYC Possible JNB-LAX NOT Possible FRA-SAO NOT Possible

Example: when placing a case on support, for the support agent to have the exact instructions from the phone agent. e.g Authorisation has to be requested by support from the airline, Policy clarification is needed. ***ATTENTION*** For orders with more than one PNR (Multi,VI), where at least one of them is GDS and another is non-GDS (reissue is done by FL), you should not register errand twice. Instead, include the information in the text box "Information to FL". 1.7) “First departure of the New PNR”- The original travel date of the New PNR that needs to be issued. The purpose is to better prioritize the urgent cases from non-urgent, based on their original travelling date, when being placed on the support/ticketing queue. Only for PNRs having the original departure date in the future, this option will be filled out with the initial travel date. 1.8) “Flexible ticket if used”-If applicable, select the type of flexible ticket used. 1.8.a) Flexible ticket online: Customer purchased a flexible ticket during booking. 1.8.b) Flexible ticket post-booking: The customer purchased a flexible ticket via "My bookings" on our website. 1.8.c Flexible ticket manual sales: Customer purchased a flexible ticket through phone or email. 2) PNR information + PNR code This part of the wizard refers to the information verified in GDS by FL that needs to be transmitted to ticketing for completing the New Ticket case. (New ticket - cost on us) Fill in the mandatory information: Reason for charge, reason code, who approved the charge. 2.6) “Ticket price” - Fill in the GDS price in the issuing currency, per pax type. 2.7) “Information to FL” - Fill in your Calculation, and the price difference per pax type. 2.8) “Information to Ticketing” - Free text will be inserted only for specific cases: Reason code, Under collection. If there is nothing to be mentioned then use "-". ***ATTENTION***: The details inserted in this part of the wizard are to be used by the ticketing department to finalise the New Ticket case. For this reason, we need to insert it as shown in GDS. 3) Confirm the case New Layout: 3.1) “Total cost charged” - The total price in the customer's currency regardless of whether the customer has paid or not. 3.2) "Actions" - Select the action you wish to take. 3.3) “No queue action” - The case is informative, no payment was received, no other actions have to be taken. 3.4) “Send to ticketing” - Payment has been received and ticket issuance can be completed by the ticketing department. When selecting this option, the case will be automatically sent to the ticketing queue and in the general view, it will appear as “Placed on queue”. No need to place it in the queue once again. Only a normal errand note will be added by the agent with precise information as per the instructions here. << https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/137effd9-d6c1-4024-bb69-1edc493a5a95/?view=snippet-view&trigger=title&searchEventId=01HJ634NWS2KTK3T0AFA15G6GQ&source=shelf&DTStep=01H5PJRK1JQ01D1F3DF43AR0G7 >> 1) Create rebooking case - Common information 1.1) “Scenario”- Select New Ticket. 1.2) “Name of customer contact” - The person the agent interacts with. 1.3) “Select travelers”- 1.3.a) If the New Ticket is for already existing passenger, select his/her name. 1.3.b) If the New Ticket is for a new passenger select the "+" and insert his/her name (ALWAYS First name and then Last name). 1.4) “Select PNR”- PNR to be issued. *Make sure to ALWAYS link the new PNR before creating the rebooking case" 1.5) “Add on purchase”- When there is a paid payment link related to the New Ticket case, you need to connect it to the case. 1.6) “Information to FL” - Specific information that needs to be provided ONLY to FL. Example: when placing a case on support, for the support agent to have the exact instructions from the phone agent. e.g Authorisation has to be requested by support from the airline, Policy clarification is needed. ***ATTENTION*** For orders with more than one PNR (Multi,VI), where at least one of them is GDS and another is non-GDS (reissue is done by FL), you should not register errand twice. Instead, include the information in the text box "Information to FL". 1.7) “First departure of the New PNR”- The original travel date of the New PNR that needs to be issued. The purpose is to better prioritize the urgent cases from non-urgent, based on their original travelling date, when being placed on the support/ticketing queue. Only for PNRs having the original departure date in the future, this option will be filled out with the initial travel date. 1.8) “Flexible ticket if used”-If applicable, select the type of flexible ticket used. 1.8.a) Flexible ticket online: Customer purchased a flexible ticket during booking. 1.8.b) Flexible ticket post-booking: The customer purchased a flexible ticket via "My bookings" on our website. 1.8.c Flexible ticket manual sales: Customer purchased a flexible ticket through phone or email. 2) PNR information + PNR code This part of the wizard refers to the information verified in GDS by FL that needs to be transmitted to ticketing for completing the New Ticket case. In case multiple PNRs are selected, this page has to be filled separately for each PNR. Once you complete the information for the first PNR and click on next, then the same page will appear for the second one. 2.1) “Scenario”-New ticket 2.2) “Flights” - The new flights 2.3) “GDS pricing command” - The actual command performed in GDS. 2.4) “Ancillary EMD" - For EMD that has to be added. 2.5) “Ticket Type”-Select the respective option, according to your scenario. 2.5.a) New tkt sell 2.5.b) Flx tkt 2.5.c) Void &Rbk 2.5.d) Compl. (New ticket - cost on us) Fill in the mandatory information: Reason for charge, reason code, who approved the charge. 2.6) “Ticket price” - Fill in the GDS price in the issuing currency, per pax type. 2.7) “Information to FL” - Fill in your Calculation, and the price difference per pax type. 2.8) “Information to Ticketing” - Free text will be inserted only for specific cases: Reason code, Under collection. If there is nothing to be mentioned then use "-". ***ATTENTION***: The details inserted in this part of the wizard are to be used by the ticketing department to finalise the New Ticket case. For this reason, we need to insert it as shown in GDS. 3) Confirm the case New Layout: 3.1) “Total cost charged” - The total price in the customer's currency regardless of whether the customer has paid or not. 3.2) "Actions" - Select the action you wish to take. 3.3) “No queue action” - The case is informative, no payment was received, no other actions have to be taken. 3.4) “Send to ticketing” - Payment has been received and ticket issuance can be completed by the ticketing department. When selecting this option, the case will be automatically sent to the ticketing queue and in the general view, it will appear as “Placed on queue”. No need to place it in the queue once again. Once the case has been sent to the ticketing department, FL should not update any information inserted. 3.4.a) “Mark as urgent”- PNRs that need to be issued with priority can be marked as urgent. This option will be used only for specific scenarios. e.g. new flights are within a few hours, limited ticketing period from the airline. - "Urgent due to carrier rule policy": For cases where we have strict deadlines according to the airline's policy. Ticketing team SLA is 4 hours. - "Marks the case as urgent for ticketing": For all other urgent reasons, where the ticketing should be completed within less than 4 hours. Ticketing team SLA is 2 hours. Please note that following this, a pop-up message will appear indicating that the order has been successfully placed on the Ticketing queue: 3.5) “Change order state”- When sending to ticketing, FL can change the order status as well, depending on the scenario. E.g New Ticket, Against Flexible ticket etc. Please note, if the order has already been changed you will still need to unchange and change the order, regardless if it is for the same reason. After confirming the unchange of the order you may select the change reason based on your scenario. Edvin will always update the latest date of the change: 3.6) “Register errand” - Fill in the boxes as per the current process. Important! It is very important that before sending to the ticketing team, make sure that all actions are completed in GDS (segments and TST are saved). Kindly use the "IGNORE AND REDISPLAY " command (IR) in GDS in order to be sure that the YY locator is provided and segments are still confirmed.

question: how to check status of claims and payouts
ground_truth: Status of claims and payouts The purpose of this page is to help Frontline have a better insight into the progress and priorities for refunds that the BO team is working on. The information on this page can help with the calls/email handling, complaints and for us all to be aligned on the information provided to our customers. Back office has split the refund process into two steps: 1) Claim = when we make the refund in GDS/BSP 2) Payout = when we make the refund to the customer The above are at different stages currently because we do not make any pre-payments. We make the claim, then we wait to receive the amount from the airline, and only when we receive the amount in our account we will make the payout to the customer. The progress for both steps can be found below: The current refund priorities for Back Office are: B.com Service Package (Premium and Platinum) US/UK/CA/DK markets Klarna Sensitive airlines Chargebacks FOP Cash Chargebacks Old orders (based on queue placement date) Order value over 3000 EUR Order value 1500-3000 EUR

question: how to recognize if the ryanair pnr is cc2c
ground_truth: As in all the CC2C orders, you will be able to identify if this Ryanair PNR is sold as CC2C through them relevant banner, which will include the Ryanair PNR. The criteria that we are followed so that an order can be considered CC2C for Ryanair are the below: 1. Only for One Way/ Return trips and will not be used in OWC or VI . 2. Only Card payment can be used. We cannot support CC2C functionality for Google Wallets, Apple Wallets, Klarna etc. 3. The only cards that are eligible also in FR website are VI, MC, AX, DS, Diners. No discounts apply. 4. System used should be Travelfusion. 5. We will not be issuing CC2C Ryanair orders for Booking.com. If any of these criteria above is not valid, then we will use the usual ETG methods (VAN cards). Customers will be informed in case the currency needs to be changed in the payment page, prior to any payment being completed. In the confirmation page and email as well as the invoice the charges for ETG and for Ryanair will be shown separately. The same information will be shown in the Edvin Order overview. Price to customer: Total price paid from the customer. Amount paid: Describes the amount paid to ETG. CC2Carrier Amount: Describes the amount paid to the airline.

question: steps for manual calculation for partially used tickets
ground_truth: Steps for manual calculation for partially used tickets: 1. After selecting the new segments we can proceed with the command WFRTR2¥AQR¥N1.1¥S7-9 instead of FQP in Amadeus. 2.The outbound trip is marked as F(Flown). We fill in the CODE boxes with X for the inbound trip and the same (X) in NEXT box so as to continue. 3. In PRICE-P/MANUAL-M box insert P so that the system prices automatically take into consideration the historical data of the used outbound segments. 4. Insert in NEXT box X. 5. Here is our calculation of ticket difference. We fill in the CHG FEE AMOUNT as per fare rules (airline's PENALTY) and click in NEXT box X. Note: Note: If the currency is different in the fare rule from the one of the PCC (mentioned also under REISSUE column, next to CUR), then we need to convert the currency as per ticketing office currency. Important! As we need to fill in the exact tax difference (tax by tax) in the Rebooking wizard for manual calculation (partially used for this scenario), if we notice that there is a tax difference (from TTL TAXES), we should click on "TAX COMPARISON" in order to see each tax in detail, and specify them on the Rebooking Wizard-related page (Manual Rebooking). 6. We fill in the NEW TKT FULL COMM AMT & ADD COLL COMM AMT just 0, also we can see the baggage allowance of 02 pc if it is priced with baggage, and the Fulfillment team (TKT) will fix it later. We also select the Form of Payment always CASH and click in RETAIN box X. After retaining the transaction if we do IR the stored fare will not be saved, hence if we want to store the fare we need to enter ER to store the fare. Note: We do ER ONLY when the passenger agrees to the changes and we have received the payment from the passenger. 7. Now, to see the details of the calculation performed by the agent on Sabre, as well as the Fare Basis for the new segments and new taxes breakdown, use the command *PQS and select the RETAINED REISSUE mask with the command *PQRx, where x corresponds to the mask number, 2 in the below screenshot. Also, we do not need to perform manual calculations on our own.

question: step by step new ticket sell when existing ticket the requested change is not permitted
ground_truth: Amadeus - step by step New Ticket Sell a) In the existing ticket the requested change is not permitted any of the ticket rules does not allow reissue (changes not permitted, destination change not allowed, stop over not allowed, max stay regulations, etc) original ticket is changeable and you have offered customer a rebooking, but customer thinks this is too expensive and is looking for a new ticket, either on same flight or different flight/airline: 1) Clone the existing PNR’s passengers’ details using command RRP. The name of the passenger(s), phone number, e-mail address, remarks with order information will be copied. 2) Use FXD command to view the best available connections: FXDLON/D23DECKRS/R,UP Where: LON is airport of departure, 23DEC is the date of the departure, KRS is the destination airport To find ONE WAY cost for all the passengers(according to their type as well) in the PNR with all the airlines, including negotiated fares: FXDLON/D23DECKRS/D30DECLON/R,UP To find ROUND TRIP cost for all the passengers(according to their type as well) in the PNR with all the airlines, including negotiated fares: FXDLON/D23DECKRS/D03JANLON//ASK/R,UP To find ROUND TRIP cost for all the passengers (according to their type as well) in the PNR with the SPECIFIC airline(SK), including negotiated fares. If you need connection with more than one carrier add following airline codes after a comma (//ASK, LH) Example In the display you can see the total cost for all the passengers, exact flights and booking class/farebasis, as well as baggage allowance. Also, you can see FX commands and the action that will be performed. In order to select a higher fare that would include baggage, you can use FXY1, where 1 is the option number from the displayed list (in this case it is only one). ground_truth: Death situations - Russian Law Tickets to/from/via Russia with Russian airlines: Some customers refer to Russian law for a refund of their flight tickets in medical and/or death situations. question: how to handle exceptional rebooking scenarios
ground_truth: Exceptional rebooking scenarios per airline United Airlines (UA) Unused refunds: We have identified an issue where a large number of United Airlines (UA) tickets have been refunded as Unused (NSR), while the customers had actually left the tickets open for future use. A set of instructions was created to handle these tickets, and the orders that are eligible for this handling have been marked with a specific errand note (see Step 1). Note: We are not taking proactive actions for these orders; instead, we will be handling each case when/if the customers contact us on their own. Handling steps: 1) Confirm that it is a UA NSR affected order via the errand/ note 2) Explain to the customer that the booking was canceled and automatically handled as an old order by our system, however we can offer a discount code for the entire value of the UA tickets with specific criteria (see 2.b.) 2.1) Use the following script: "I see that your departure was scheduled for [XX] months ago. Unfortunately, we didn’t hear from you on how to proceed with your reservation. Therefore, your booking was canceled and automatically handled as an old order by our system. I understand you’d like to rebook your trip and I am happy to help. To solve the issue, I can offer you a discount code for the entire value of the ticket, which can be used to book your trip with the same airline, and follow the same policies offered by the carrier for your original ticket. Please note that this code is provided by us and can only be used on <BRAND> website where you made your original booking." 2.2) Voucher criteria: 2.2.a) Voucher must used at the website the original ticket was bought from, and must be used once (i.e. cannot use part of the voucher amount now and the rest later) 2.2.b) Voucher amount must be the total TKT value for UA PNR (not the whole order in case of multi-PNR orders), and only one voucher will be issued per order and for all passengers 2.2.c) Carrier must be United Airlines (UA) 2.2.d) Travel must begin before 31-12-2022 2.2.e) Travel must be completed until 31-12-2023 3) In order to have the voucher issued and sent to the customer, use the RL Jira due to Other<< https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/ca0ee407-2afd-47d5-ac0a-f5b5be644cb5?DTStep=QIYljW-Dig >> step-by-step instructions to request the reason code, with the following details: 3.1) The Jira type should always be Other 3.2) The Jira should be assigned to Birgitta Gustavsson 3.3) Mention in the description clearly that it is a UA NSR case and make sure that the amount of the discount voucher is equal to the total UA TKT value for the order (only for United Airlines tickets) The Manager/TL/Supervisor (for the time being Birgitta) will approve and create the discount voucher. The RL Jira will have reason code "NSR Process" and Resolution note "UA NSR + free text" 3.4) After the voucher is created, follow the rest of the RL Jira routine as normal Note: 1) The above steps apply for Inhouse and Support agents. 2) Outsourcing agents should use the Service desk routine << https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/61d4beff-add3-400b-bb14-2a85a547f162 >> to make the request. question: steps to verify and escalate fare hikes during the initial booking
ground_truth: What is fare hike ? Fare hike is considered wherever a passenger purchasing a ticket on our website and the price might be changed. When the price changes during the booking process, the flow will be interrupted, and a message will be presented to the customer. The message shown will inform them that the price has increased from x amount to z, and will look like the message below: Following this message and in order to be able to know internally that this was indeed presented to the customer, and he accepts the fare hike, an Order note will also be added automatically (errand under the Base/Bookings tab) along with the log OrderNote under __ Events and logs -> Merged Events Logs. The errand under the Base/Bookings tab will look like this: The OrderNote _ under _ Merged Events Logs will look like this: Useful information: 1. Clicking on "Back to payment", will remove this message and update the payment page with the new payable amount, without submitting the page. This means, that if the customer clicks on "Accept new price", the booking will be processed, if s/he clicks on "Back to payment" the payment page will be updated and the customer can either quit or process the payment/booking. 2. The message is not a pop-up that could be blocked by browser settings. 3. Is there any reason the message would not appear? The answer here is that anything that can go wrong in loading the page e.g. user's internet is down etc, would prevent the message from loading. But in those cases, we won't proceed to actually make a booking as the customer wouldn't accept the price change 4. There is currently no way to determine whether the customer clicked on "Accept new price" or on "Back to payment", but we can just review whether he continued because we would get an order afterward. Important to note is that orders coming through the Booking.com are not affected by this development. This means that these orders will have neither an errand nor a log showing the price change, however, according to Booking.com this topic is covered internally, and the change is always shown to the customers. How to check Fare hike, if there is no errand note in the order (as mentioned above): If the customer contact us claiming there was no information about a fare hike, or a fare hike they did not confirm, or chosen “Back to payment” and still got a booking and there is no errand note in the order, please do as follow: Always check what passenger paid (Air) Open Events and Logs -> Price History Start site price : is what passenger saw during the booking End site price: is what passenger was charged eventually 1. Check if “start site price” and “end site price” are the same. 1.1 If yes, then there is no fare hike. 1.2 If not, then there is a fare hike, inform the customer we will investigate and get back. 2. Check if “End site price” is the same with “Air”. 2.1 If yes, then escalate to manager 2.2 If not, then escalate to SS. How to escalate: For Outcoursing companies: Open ticket through Service Desk. For In-house team: Insert relevant notes and open jira to “Retail Loss (RL)” project as tech error. 1. Once your manager approves the cost, raise a contact form to SL payouts through etrack by selecting the category "Additional Payout". 2. Register errand: Category 6: Payment questions, Type: 9: Fare hike

question: how can you check the status of a refund request after submission
ground_truth: Cancellation and refund For cancellation and void, follow the below: Refund Post-ticketing Service Team Please visit FR24 B2B portal https://www.flightroutes24.com and log in with your username and password. Submit your request of reissue/refund/name correction by clicking on the buttons in Order Details page. For Instructions: Find info at Service Center – Help Center on B2B website https://b2b.flightroutes24.com/view/service/help.html Contact Customer Support using Web Chat Tool on B2B portal to consult any post ticketing issues; Email for consulting After.sales@flightroutes24.com Portal Request Submission: 24 / 7 Web Chat Tool & Email: 9am to 10pm everyday General information: There are two inquiry refund types, for confirm to refund the segments will be cancelled and the ticket cannot be used. Also, after you click submit, there will be a pop-up window to notify you the seat will be canceled. In case of 24 hour cancellation rule request you may use the same process, but insert in the notes your comment that we would like to know if the carrier supports this process so that FR24 can check and let us know if refund under better conditions can be provided. NEVER confirm to the customer that the full refund is guaranteed as each airline treats this scenario case to case policy. For Quoting refund fee only, which is only a option for voluntary refund, FR24 only checks the available refund amount for you and won't cancel the segments, the passenger can normally use the ticket. In general, FR24 sets 30 min timeline for reschedule quote as reschedule fee may change any time regarding its cabin and fare left. However, for voluntary refund, except the request that close to departure, we will set longer time, more than 30 min for Quoting refund fee only. Because the available refund fee will change regarding fare basis, like request for 7 days before departure and request for 2 days before departure may be different, so we usually set timeline within the day you submit. A. Search for the order you want to refund: 1. Select 'Ticket Tracking' in the left navigation bar. 2. Find the order you want to refund from 'Ticketing completed' tab. 3. Click on the 'Order No.' B. Refund details: 1. Click on 'Refund' button in the 'Passenger information section on order details. C. Review and confirm details: 1. Select the passenger that you have received confirmation to refund. 2. Select the refund reason. 3. Select refund method 4. Click on 'Submit'. D. Refund successfully processing 1. Once you have followed the instructions above the pop-up below will appear to you. Click on 'OK' when you submit successfully. E. Review your refund request 1. Click on 'Refund Management' in the menu shown on the left side of your page. 2. Find your refund request from the 'Refund applied' tab and check the status or any other details required. F. Confirm refund amount 1. FR24 calculates the refund according to the airline's policy and changes the status of the refund request to 'Refund amount TBC'. 2. If you agree with the amount click on 'Confirm'. The amount you confirmed will be refunded from FR24. 3. If you do not agree with the amount calculated, click on 'Dispute' and FR24 will review the case and contact back. G. Check the status of refund 1. In the tab shown above the applications sent, locate the tab 'Refund Completed' to see the amount refunded to the designated account. ATTENTION: Please note that in case the customer has requested refund directly from the airline, the request does not reflect in the FR24 portal and FR24 cannot see it as well, unless they are informed from the airline. In case FR24 informs us that the customer has processed the refund directly with the airline or the customer informs us that they have processed the refund with the airline, we still need to run the refund process within the portal so that the payment can be processed to us.

question: force majeure manual rebooking calculation when your booking is purged but the ticket is open
ground_truth: Manuel calculation when your booking is purged but the ticket is open When your booking is purged, but the ticket is open, you need to make a new PNR. You should be able to go ahead and do this with an ATC. You can use both Amadeus and Sabre tickets and make the new PNR in Amadeus. You will find the ticket number in Edvin or in the history of the ticke This is the ticket and the status is open. Create a new PNR, adding some mandatory field Name: NM1EKLUND/LARS MR (If more than one name NM1EKLUND/LARS MR 1EKLUND/LENA MRS) Email: APE-LARS@GMAIL.COM Phone: APM-+467025555555 Ticketing arrangement element: TKOK Before adding the ticket number you need to add the new itinerary. Add the ticket number: >FHE117-3853213260 Now you can go ahead and do your ATC command. FXO/R,UP and you will find the reissue image. Then just 'ER' and charge the customer if any payment needed or send the new PNR to ticketing for issue. **Remember always to link the PNR in Edvin. (For an EMD-number just add it with FHDxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxxx, for instance a voucher or a bag.) If an ATC is not working just go ahead with doing a manual calculation, in this case using FXX, and compare it with the original ticket. If a manual calculation is needed, always remember to check the fare rules or the TA pages.

question: force majeure manual rebooking calculation when ticket has extended validity
ground_truth: Manual calculation when ticket has extended validity When you need to make a manual calculation, and the validity of your ticket is extended according to TA, but you can't find any prices to compare with when you're backdating with FXX or FQP. Most tickets are only val for 1 year maximum so in these cases you need to make a fake return to find a price. This is a ticket where the outbound is flown, the ticket was issued 06apr2 Let's pretend you want to rebook the inbound to 28 Apr next year You pick the same booking class as in the original ticket or the first available to the left, in this case, T-classs. Then use the command FXX/r,up,06apr21/s2,3,6,7 for historical pricing (Backdating) And this is the error message you get: This is because the ticket was issued on 06 Apr and only valid for 1 year. Since the ticket was issued on 06 Apr we need to make a fake inbound for a date as close as possible before that date to get a valid price. You will pick the same booking class as you had available on the requested flig 28 Apr, so in this case T-class. Then use the command FXX/r,up,06apr21/s2,3,6,7 for historical pricing (Back dating) And this is the result you get: Now you can go ahead and do the manual calculation comparing the original ticket with the pricing for the fake return price image. Remember to be very clear in your notes when sending this to Ticketing.

question: force majeure manual rebooking calculation for a nego fare ticket
ground_truth: Manual calculation for a nego fare ticket When you need to make a manual calculation, and your ticket is in nego fare, missing fare and total. This is the ticket and it was issued 03jun21: Let's pretend you want to rebook this inbound to 20 JUN: The ATC is not working, and you need to continue with a manual calculation. You will then use the command FXP/R,U/S2,3 (instead of R,UP you will just add R,U to get the “unpublished” prices, called nego fares.). A nego ticket has to be rebooked to another nego price (there are exceptions, TK for instance) This will be your result: Since we don't have the fare of the original ticket, then you need to check the TST with the command TQT. If you get this error message, you need to proceed to the TST history with the command TTH. NO ACTIVE TST - DELETED TST RECORDS MAY EXIST - PLEASE USE TTH In the TST history, you will find all pricing details for the original ticket, and you can go ahead doing your manual calculating comparing old ticket price and today price. This is also possible to use when a PNR is purged, just use RPP/RLC-XXXXXX and then RPP/TTH

question: how to reset password or client id (cid)
ground_truth: Reset password or Client Id (CID) Please note that you can reset your own password or Client ID in travelport. question: what are the wrap-up codes (genesys email workflow)
ground_truth: Wrap-up codes Genesys email interactions are considered finalized only when you reply to the customer and select a wrap-up. The available wrap-up codes are: 1) Transferred To be used when the email interaction has been transferred to a different Genesys email Queue for handling. 2) Escalated To be used when we have informed the customer that the case has been forwarded to our Support team and has been placed in one of our Edvin Support Queues. 3) Prioritized To be used for: 3.1) Void/24-hour rule cases. 3.2) When a customer contacts us by mail for cancellation with departure within 3 days and it is possible to cancel the booking against a fee. 3.3) For rebookings due to FM or tickets close to the expiration date where the change should be completed within 3 days. 3.4) When handling voluntary cancellation requests for tickets that expire within 3 days. When a customer contacts us by mail for all the scenarios above, the agent shall first try to contact the customer by phone to assist. 3.5) Agents will make the attempt to contact the client and try to assist in EN. If the passenger can communicate then the case can be finalized in that step. 3.6) If the client can not understand EN, then the agents must send a fixed template (1 per scenario ) with the request to the passenger to contact us via phone instead. ***Important: If the customer clearly requests cancellation and a full refund is granted as per Edvin Covid-19 Docs then proceed with the modify order without waiting for the customer’s consent, disconnect the interaction and send conf of cxl through Edvin. *** A. How to proceed when the customer confirms the cxl: The agent disconnects the email interaction and sends confirmation of cxl through Edvin, Runs Modify order, and registers an errand with ‘Mail in’ where it is clearly stated that the customer was contacted by phone to confirm the cancellation. B. How to proceed if there is no answer by the customer on the phone. The agent replies to the Genesys email and adds a sentence that we have tried to reach the customer by phone without any answer. - For rebookings due to FM or tickets close to the expiration that changes need to be completed within less than 48 hours: Reply to the customer to reach us by phone a maximum of 12 hours before the deadline given by the airline and use the wrap-up Prioritized. - For voluntary cancellation requests on tickets that are close to the expiration date and the ticket can be canceled against a fee. a) If the customer’s request reached us in less than 3 days but more than 24 hours before the expiration date and the cxl can be done against a fee (by fare rules), inform the customer regarding the airline’s penalty, our handling fees and give a deadline to confirm the cancellation (maximum 24 hours before the tkt expiration date), use the Wrap-up Prioritized. b) If the customer’s request reached us in less than 24 hours before the expiration date and the cxl can be done against a fee then inform the customer regarding the airline's fees, our handling fees, advise to reach us by phone (maximum 12 hours before the tkt exp date) to confirm the cxl and use the Wrap-up Prioritized. C. How to proceed if the passenger answers the phone but does not confirm the cancellation The agent answers the email according to the above routines and adds the wrap-up prioritized. How to proceed when the customer confirms the cxl for tickets that expire within 3 days: i) If the ticket expires within 72 hours then disconnect the interaction, run modify order, send conf of cxl through Edvin and use the label 'Expiring within 72 hrs'. ii) If the customer has confirmed the cxl after the expiration date then inform the customer that he/she is not entitled to a refund. question: what is the policy for internal recategorization(genesys email workflow)
ground_truth: General Information 1) All agents are expected to check the communication hub while handling emails and close any already handled/dupe interactions. 2) Email cases/Interactions pushed to the agent; no manual picking from queues 3) Emails and phone calls are treated and measured the same way - as Interactions 4) Always insert a retention line/ghost line when the customer contacts us for any request, if not already inserted. If it is a Multi PNR and we only handle the LCC booking/ Portal booking, we still need to add a Ghostline in the GDS PNR. 5) One queue for all channels; no specific email que 6) Agents will receive a mix of phone and email interactions unless skills are changed on the agent level 7) Genesys detects language from text and routes it to the corresponding queue 8) Edvin API will give higher priority to orders with departure within 3 days 9) 1 active email interaction at a time 10) Agents will place email interactions on Edvin support when a case needs further investigation, but email always needs to be responded to with the correct template 11) No internal recategorization 12) Cases that need handling by our Schedule Change department will be transferred to the Schedule Change Queues accordingly, same way as we do with phone call interactions. See below for more details on the SC transferring. 13) Time displayed is the local time of the agent 14) Always reply in English if the customer has written in English no matter what market he/she has booked on 15) Always offer an alternative option when the customer's initial request is not possible - when applicab Some examples... 15.1) Customer emails to cancel their flight due to FM but we have no TA policy. Offer cancellation as per rules as an alternative 15.2) Customer needs a naco/nach but it is not allowed on the ticket. Offer cancellation as per fare rules if ticket is refundable and book a new ticket 15.3) Customer emails to cancel their booking due to FM, but the ticket is non-refundable, check the TA on if an open ticket or a voucher option can be offer 16) We do not handle Voluntary Rebooking requests over email - the customer must phone in. 17) Always make sure that the order number is stated in the subject field, if the order number is not stat but we have received it in the email from the customer the agent should add it in the subject fiel 18) Always reply to all the customer queries.

question: how to send a new email from genesys
ground_truth: Emails 1) Do we need to add a conversation ID to the errand note? Where to find and how to copy a conversation ID? 2) Can we search for an email? We can only search for closed email interactions and not new ones. The only way to search is by having the conversation id. More info about how to search can be found here. 3) How to send a new email from Genesys? There is no possibility to send a new email from Genesys. We are handling email threads in Genesys, and some departments such as SC agents are using either E Track or Edvin for the First email sendouts. Responses will enter Genesys and handled from there. 4) Where to find templates? In Genesys, we have Canned responses. They are available only in case an interaction is open. 5) When transferring a case, could we add a note for the other department, by clicking on a note symbol? No need to do so, just register errand by always including the conversation id 6) What should be done when the email interaction is already handled? i)Register errand under: 21: Already Handled/Incorrect Department 39: Already Handled/Incorrect Department 1: Already Handled 1: Mail In 7) Do we use Genesys for urgent refund requests to BO? No, the urgent refund requests are sent to BO either by using labels or by etrack as per our already set processes. More information can be found here-- Section 12 8)How to escalate a case to the TL? The email cannot be forwarded to the TL. The agent needs to: 8.1) reply that the request has been forwarded 8.2)register errand by always including the conversation id while the interaction is still open. 8.3)proceed as per our already set processes. 9) How to add an attachment via the new contact form? The customer is not able to add an attachment via our new contact form. The agent needs to reply to the email interaction and ask the customer to attach any document needed. If the case concerns GDPR docs that should be handled by CR or BO then redirect to : https://www.etraveligroup.com/medcert/ 10) Which tool to use when we need to contact the airline? Always etrack. 11) How to handle cases that need to be placed on support? Place Order on the respective queue in Edvin as usual and send a template to the passenger that the Support team will get back. Always include conversation id in the Errand. 12) Do we offer rebooking via email? If yes, in which case? We offer rebooking via email only for FM/SC cases. 13) Do we send payment links from Edvin or Genesys? While on call --> Edvin. question: what is the target group for gordian to fulfill the bag and seats
ground_truth: General process UPDATE: Seating fulfillment (seating light/ map & besides) has started since on February 2023 for LCC carriers throu Travelfusion and Tripstact. Gordian is a new partner that will try to fulfill the bag and seats that could not be automatically issued by the system a they have fallen to our Manual queues. In version 1, we will start with the luggage and only a few sites until we make sure everything goes as expected. Target group : Gordian will undertake the fulfillment for the LCC carriers and VI bookings (GDS + LCC). NDC carrie (portals) are excluded. Due to some restrictions, Gordian will fulfill the luggage for specific carriers either for GDS or for With 21APR22 as an expected starting date, Gordian will fulfill the luggage for VI orders before ending up in the Manu queue in Edvin. If they fail, the order will be automatically placed in the Manual queue. For pure LCC orders, fulfillment will be executed by Gordian if the system fails and can not issue the bag. If Gordian also fail the order will be automatically placed in the Manual queue, at which point agents will take over. Associated queues :"LCC Ancillary" and manual queues of VI. Those queues are handled by the SL. 1) The SLA will be 3 hours. When the luggage is successfully completed, an indication appears in Edvin indicating for which PNR the luggage was added and for which segments. 2) We do not send orders to Gordian where the departure is within 12 hours. 3) Gordian does not send a confirmation email to custome 4) If the baggage is not added successfully, the order will be placed automatically on the Manual queue in Edvin, so the SL will either try to manually add the bag or will place it to the Refund Dashboard, so that the Payout team will process the refund to the customer. (only the baggage value) Do not inform the customer that the baggage is added by an external Partner. This is something between us and Gordian and the customer is not aware of.

question: what kind of reimbursements will we disburse through hyperwallet

This could happen because the original payment details may have expired (most likely because it has been more than a year since their original booking date), or because the customer’s bank account is no longer active. Such Customer details will be sent to Hyperwallet for further processing. Before the Customer receives the first email from Hyperwallet, they will receive an email from ETG and also an SMS where we ask them to check this email and look out for Hyperwallet emails from @hyperwallet.com: See below for an email example of an email sent to a Customer: SUBJECT LINE: Important information regarding your refund for [booking number] Hi, [CUSTOMER NAME] We are writing to inform you that we are unable to process a refund of [AMOUNT CURRENCY] for booking number [BOOKING NUMBER] on your original payment method. This is likely because it has been more than one year since your original booking date. To process your refund, we require your updated credit card details. We will contact you within 2-7 business days from an email with @hyperwallet.com as the domain Please note Hyperwallet is a trusted partner, powered by PayPal. It is a user-friendly payment platform that allows us to quickly distribute funds across 170+ countries in more than 150 currencies Included in this email will be a link where you can update your credit card details and claim your funds To access the form you will also be asked to verify your account by validating your phone number. Please use the number you provided when booking your trip. If you can’t remember what number you entered when making your booking, please follow these steps: Open your confirmation email Click “My Bookings” Scroll down to “Important information for your trip” Here you will find the right telephone number. Type only the digits to answer the validating question, don't type the "+" After verification, you will be able to access the form to provide your details. Once completed, you will be refunded within 6 business days As previously mentioned, you will receive the validation email from @hyperwallet.com within 2-7 days and we kindly ask you to wait for this email before contacting us again Please note that the amount you receive is your flight refund excluding any non-refundable additional services (such as check-in service, seating service etc.) and any fees that were agreed on upon cancelling your reservation. Thank you, [BRAND NAME]

question: why is wfrf not working
ground_truth: Why is WFRF not working? 1) An earlier SC on the booking/involuntary reissue 2) Airline is not connected to WFRF (WFRF ENTRY NOT AVAILABLE ) 3) Category VC / 31 not loaded in the rules 4) Price found in a ghost area where WFRF not possible 5) Not always possible on unpublished price 6) We do not follow rules such as penalty (PE), routing (RG/RTG) or flight application (FL/FA) 7) Price is broken at another point than the destination
context: Sabre ATC (WFRF) 1) Make sure you are in the right area. It should be the main area/ PCC as the ticket is issued in, (*S - To display area you are in); SE 1ADA - Z9EC NO 08LA - 4NZ7 DK C73B - P65B FI A99B - X45B NL 2BPB - W1ZC 2) If we have an infant in PNR please check DOB to see, if the infant will still be an infant after the rebooking. 3) Add the new requested segment(s) without saving. question: step by step check fare rules and cancel
ground_truth: Step by Step - Check fare rules and Cancel - Amadeus Amadeus 1) Open PNR in respective office id, use RT+PNR 2) Check Ticket status (O or A) in the ticket line. Use RTTN or RTF to open the ticket line. TWD/L1 to open ticket on line 1. 3) Check the penalties for all fare basis on the ticket. For detailed steps please refer here<< https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/099b9fac-cdb3-4d9f-b904-e20b80ca9e56 >>. 4) If nothing is mentioned in fare rules and documents, take the most restrictive penalty within the entity (pricing unit or fare component). More information can be found here<< https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/c5520e56-7b43-443e-87b2-7c12e5c6c98e >>. 5) Inform the passenger about the airline penalty converted in pax currency using the Order creation date along with our Refund fee. All fees are per person. 6) If the passenger confirms cancellation, delete segments. 7) If he confirms: Modify the order in Edvin, selecting the correct reason (Ticket rules-airline fee) 8) No need to register an errand again. Modify order already includes that. 9) Send respective confirmation email from Edvin. 10) If the ticket's rule is non-refundable, then we just inform the passenger that the ticket is non-refundable. Nothing else. Only if a passenger asks for taxes then we could check after deducting our tax refund fee if something will remain. In this case, we will inform the passenger about our fee without giving any calculation or exact refund amount. We will inform you that BO makes the calculation as some taxes may not be refunded in this case. Only if the customer is entitled to a refund after deducting our fee we will Modify order. General: If a ticket was exchanged, usually you need to check the original ticket and insert the original ticket issue date in your command. If the ticket is partially used you usually need to check the ''After departure'' section of the rules, unless otherwise specified. question: how ryanair pnrs sold through letsfly
ground_truth: Ryanair PNRs sold through Letsfly Ryanair does not provide support to travel agencies. question: how to handle reviews on trustpilot
ground_truth: Handling of the reviews The reviews are separated as per below: If the volume that needs to be handled is not excessive, you can skip the filtering per review category and reply accordingly as per the instructions. Select 'Star rating' to filter the category you will be working on. Only 1-3 star reviews should be handled and we must respond to them. 1) Do not filter ‘Great’/ ‘Excellent’ reviews(4-5 stars) no response is needed 2) Continue with the 'Bad/ Poor' reviews: 2.1) If there is no order number, we request booking details and leave an errand in ‘Register New Errand’ inserting only the name and the type of request. 2.2) If there is an order number or any booking details or Trustpilot reference, make the investigation normally and reply to the customer. Use the reference on the right to open order in Edvin. (Usually reviews come after the event the customer refers to.) 2.3) For requests on refund delays through Trustpilot, we have no special priority other than in the normal requests. If a case needs to be escalated to SL, use the same errand path as in the other requests. 2.4) We never send a direct apology to the reviews as any reply of such can be used legally against us. All the replies have generic phrasing and wording. You could use the phrase though 'We are sorry you are dissatisfied with the service provided. 3) 'Average reviews'- Usually it is not possible to reply through a template. If there is a request we reply the same way we do on the bad reviews or if it has a positive tone you can thank them. Once you reply to the review, you must select a tag based on the request you handled. Only one tag can be seen, if more than one tag is inserted, then only the first is taken into consideration. If the customer's review needs additional handling such as contacting the customer due to our mishandling or any other objection that can be turned around make sure to add it to the queue by using the correct errand path as stated here<< https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/fc48adda-0ee6-45bf-94ae-2677f6c8c8e6?parentId=8527c4a5-637f-4c26-8206-801df9faf560&view=card-view&trigger=title&searchEventId=01HE2GWP6QXWV4WWGDTVJ131V9&source=shelf&DTStep=01G27B49JB21R1NG758B91J6EV >> and then place it on the correct Support queue in Edvin. Please note this is possible only if the customer mentions the order or PNR nr in their review. Until further notice, please avoid using the 'Report' button, unless the comment sent is very aggressive and racist. Critical thinking should always be used in such cases. When we report a review, the Trustpilot team investigates the reporting and informs us via an email in case they approve the report or not. If the report is approved the review gets deleted and so is the rating. ATTENTION: You should be reporting reviews as 'Harmful or illegal' if they are threatful towards a company's individual. Once the incident has been reported to Trustpilot, it is also very important that you report it to your Manager as well. Guidelines for the Support agents When an order is sent to Support for further investigation and handling, the Support agents are supposed to check the errands and handle the case based on the standard routines of Support. All the guidelines can be found under FL Support.<< https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/0728947f-dc1b-451d-9920-c1d042c59aaf/?searchEventId=01HZPJR8C0CHZGMTFN43K8GDHV&source=shelf&trigger=title&view=snippet-view >> Once the Support agent calls the customer and solves the case with them, the Support agent should also propose to the customer to adjust their review and rating on Trustpilot.

question: What are the Paid seating terms and conditions (Availability)
ground_truth: Paid seating on British Airways is subject to availability and confirmed only after payment. It’s available on British Airways flights and some operated by franchisee or codeshare partners, though terms may differ. Group bookings (9+ passengers) can only book paid seating via British Airways Group Sales, and Avios payment isn’t available for groups. Un-ticketed passengers (e.g., cruise or package holiday travelers) must confirm ticket numbers before selecting paid seating.
context: Terms and conditions Paid seating terms and conditions Availability 1. All paid seating is subject to availability and is only confirmed once paid for. 2. Paid seating is available on British Airways mainline operated flights and on British Airways-operated flights marketed by other carriers. 3. Paid seating may be offered by British Airways franchisee airlines. The seating Terms and Conditions of British Airways franchisee airlines may differ from those of British Airways mainline-operated flights, therefore we recommend that you refer to the franchisee airline’s relevant Terms and Conditions. 4. Paid seating may be unavailable on some flights operated by codeshare partners. 5. Paid seating for group customers (bookings containing more than 9 passengers) is only available where the reservation has been made directly with British Airways Group Sales. Group customers who have made their reservation through a travel agent or a tour operator cannot currently book paid seating. Payment with Avios is currently unavailable for group customers. 6. All un-ticketed passengers, including those travelling on a cruise or package holiday who have not yet received confirmation of their ticket numbers, are unable to choose paid seating until they have received confirmation of their ticket numbers.

question: What are the Paid seating terms and conditions (Changes to seats)
ground_truth: On British Airways flights, you can change your paid seat (subject to availability), but no refund is given for downgrades, and you must pay the price difference for upgrades. Changes are not allowed on flights marketed by other carriers. Paid seating is not guaranteed and may be changed for operational reasons, even after boarding. If your seat is changed, you can request a refund if you're unsatisfied. Paid seating is non-transferable.

You cannot make changes to paid seating on British Airways-operated flights marketed by other carriers. 3. Paid seating is not guaranteed, as seating may need to be changed for operational, safety or security reasons, even after boarding the aircraft. 4. Paid seating is not transferable to any other passenger.

question: What are the Paid seating terms and conditions (Refunds)
ground_truth: Paid seating is generally non-refundable, except in specific cases: if British Airways changes your seat and you’re unsatisfied, your flight is canceled, you become ineligible for an exit row (with 48 hours' notice), or you paid for a cabin upgrade but don’t want to pay for seat selection in the upgraded cabin. Refunds are not given if you cancel your flight, are involuntarily upgraded, or are unsuitable for the seat selected. Refunds also don’t apply if you accept a voucher or book a flight marketed by another carrier. Refund requests must be made within 30 days of the last flight and will be processed to the original payment method (credit card or Avios account).

question: What are the Paid seating terms and conditions (Exit row seats)
ground_truth: Exit row seats are located next to or behind the emergency exit door. To sit in an exit row, you must be over 12, not pregnant, not have accessibility needs or severe visual/hearing impairments, be physically able to operate the emergency exit, and understand English instructions. British Airways determines eligibility, and if you don’t meet the criteria, you’ll be reassigned to a different seat with no refund for the exit row seat. If your eligibility changes before the flight, contact British Airways at least 48 hours in advance for a refund.

question: what are the Information available on SCDN
ground_truth: Information on SCDN SCDN (Schedule Change Disruption Notification) is used to notify customers of a flight cancellation, schedule change or delay. Applicable for direct or trade bookings (also adds SSR OTHS for the travel agent), Groups and BA Hols. Similar message can also be sent by BA Ops Control within -48hrs disruption window. question: How are our customers messaged for schedule changes
ground_truth: Most direct customers are now messaged via our messaging provider 15below provided there are contact details in the PNR. 15below will email the customer as a primary method of communication but can also send SMS.
context: Most direct customers are now messaged via our messaging provider 15below provided there are contact details in the PNR. 15below will email the customer as a primary method of communication but can also send SMS. These messages are automatically sent once a PNR is updated and covers several scenarios: Cancellation with/without rebook Schedule Changes - Timing changes Cabin downgrades Within 72 hours or in mass disruption, we may also message customers via our legacy messaging system SCDN. SCDN will email and SMS the customer if customer details are in the PNR. The reason for using SCDN is that it allows us to message customers ahead of a flight being cancelled and captures all PNRs i.e. codeshare customers. If a customer has been messaged via 15below, this can be identified via an RM keyword i.e. RM *15BELOW* CANCELLATION NOTIFICATION EMAIL SENT SUCCESSFULLY FOR <FLT NO> < FLT DATE DD MMM YYYY> TO <EMAIL ADDRESS>, DD MMM YYYY HHMM(Z). If the customer has been messaged via SCDN, this can be identified via SK EUCN keyword or SSR OTHS keyword. question: How to identify timing changes
ground_truth: If a direct customer has a BA flight retimed, they will be automatically messaged by BA via 15below. The segment status will now be automatically updated from TK to HK once the customer has been messaged. The process followed is as per the below (please note this process was newly updated in May 2021). Sector is retimed in PNR. Sector status changes to TK. question: What is the difference between a flight delay and a schedule change (no time limit)
ground_truth: Flight delays occur on the day of travel whereas schedule changes are notified in advance and the PNR is updated.
context: Flight delays occur on the day of travel whereas schedule changes are notified in advance and the PNR is updated. Minimum deadline for rebooking before flight departure The deadline for rebooking through Contact Centres/Trade is 2hrs before flight departure. Do not book customers onto flights departing within the 2hr window as the airport teams are now in control of the flight. Travel on a through ticket We always recommend that customers travel on a through ticket. If a flight is schedule changed as part of a through ticket, any connecting flights may be rebooked or refunded following the options from the Conditions of Carriage, so if the connecting flight is operated by BA, IB or a JB partner, the rebooking options are more extensive. The rebooking options onto a non-JB route or a Prime other carrier's flight are limited to the same booking class as original. Separate tickets issued in the same booking Not possible through BA Direct channels. If a flight is schedule changed and the customer has connecting flights in the same booking but issued on separate tickets, then the rebooking and refund options are only available for the disrupted ticket. Fare rules apply for any flight changes or refunds on the separate ticket/s. Separate tickets issued in different bookings If a flight is schedule changed and the customer has 'connecting' flights but issued on separate bookings, then the rebooking and refund options are only available for the disrupted booking. Fare rules apply for any flight changes or refunds on the separate booking, even if this is for travel on BA services. Changing a return flight if the outbound has been disrupted If a customer's stay at their destination is shortened due to a disrupted outbound flight, then we allow them to involuntarily change their return leg to give them the same length of stay as their original ticket following the Conditions of Carriage guidelines. Protecting the return sector If the outbound sector has been significantly changed (> 4 hours) by BA and the customer decides to make their own way to the destination, the return sector can be protected but the ticket will need to be reissued, with the outbound sector value refunded as per Conditions of Carriage. If the customer voluntarily chooses to cancel their outbound, then the return sector can still be protected but fare rules need to be followed. The return sector will need to be re-calculated as a one-way journey and offline service fees charged.

question: How to check if a flight is cancelled
ground_truth: For a standard BA prime cancellation outside of 72 hours to departure, this can be identified via a sector with a UN status. There will also be customer messaging RM keyword from 15below messaging i.e. o RM *15BELOW* CANCELLATION NOTIFICATION EMAIL SENT SUCCESSFULLY FOR <FLT NO> < FLT DATE DD MMM YYYY> TO <EMAIL ADDRESS>, DD MMM YYYYHHMM(Z).

For further confirmation feel free to also use BA.com (Real Time Arrivals and Departures) and availability displays in GDS to check the flight is cancelled. For BA prime cancellations inside the operational window (<72 hours to departure) cancellations may present in a different way and there may not be a sector with UN status. This is because a different tool is used by Revenue Management to process these cancellations called Joint Business Re-accommodation Tool (JBR). Please see below how to identify cancellations inside 72 hours if there is no UN present and JBR tool has been used. • FX or LX followed by the text “FLT CNX” under the impacted sector in the face of the PNR returni.e. BA 112 J 15OCT 6 JFKLHR HK1 7 1830 0630+1 *1A/E*/1S /AU/C/I/CAB J/ /4/0001/ / / / FX-FLT CNX • SK EUCN keyword for the cancelled sector i.e. o SK EUCN BA BA0164/20MAY21/OPEN/N/DIRECT/18MAY21/1051/SMS/O • Re-accommodation RX keywords relating to “Passenger Reaccommodation Service” or “JBR” i.e. o RX INVOL CHG BY PASSENGER REACCOMMODATION SERVICE ROBOTIC o RX INVOL PASSENGER REACCOMMODATION SERVICE NO SOLUTION FOUND o RX *CANX BA459/10JAN* 09JAN2125/JBR REBOOKED BA459/10JAN TO IB830/11JAN/BA483/11JAN o RX *CANX BA459/10JAN* 09JAN2124/JBR NO SOLUTION FOUND • A customer messaging RM keyword from 15below messaging i.e. o RM *15BELOW* CANCELLATION NOTIFICATION EMAIL SENT SUCCESSFULLY FOR <FLT NO> < FLT DATE DD MMM YYYY> TO <EMAIL ADDRESS>, DD MMM YYYYHHMM(Z). • A customer messaging SSR OTHS keyword from SCDN (only for indirect trade) SSR OTHS 1S BA0260/28DEC20/0900/ISB CANX. EMAIL AND SMS SENT TO PASSENGER If the customer is cancelled via JBR and is not rebooked to an alternative service, then they will remain HK on the cancelled service. These customers can be managed as per a standard cancellation, however the FX-FLT CANX (or LX), EUCN keywork and RX messages must be present in the PNR. Once again there can be occasions when the Prime other carriers' flight has been cancelled but the feed through to BA hasn't been actioned yet. Check the other carrier's website for their latest Flight Status and if the flight shows cancelled add a remark and assist the customer. For Prime other carrier flights, the UN status is added by the operating carrier and this feeds through into BA's Amadeus booking. Again, if there is no UN status but the customer is saying that their flight is cancelled, check their website latest Flight Status, add a remark into the booking and assist the customer. If there is no evidence of the flight being cancelled, then for JB flights call-pass through the customer for assistance or for OneWorld check with Helpdesk or advise the customer to contact the disrupting carrier.

question: Do all exit seats have legroom

question: Are open Jaw allowed for FCOD ?

ROUTE: LON-LIN ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: YES 2. ROUTE: LON-LIN-LON ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: YES 3. ROUTE: LON-LIN//ROM-LON or LIN-LON-AMS ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: NO 4. ROUTE: MAN-LON-ROM-LON-MAN ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: NO
context: FCOD Eligibility FCOD is only available to eligible customers who have purchased a Fare Families “PLUS” or “PLUS FLEX” product. FCOD is also offered on eligible business-class tickets. The free change on the day eligibility is not mentioned within the fare rules paragraph via Pegasus. To be eligible for FCOD all of the following must be met: A Ticketed journey must be a non-stop point-to-point shorthaul or domestic journey, either one-way or round-trip (open jaws or multiple flights are not permitted- see below for examples) 1. ROUTE: LON-LIN ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: YES 2. ROUTE: LON-LIN-LON ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: YES 3. ROUTE: LON-LIN//ROM-LON or LIN-LON-AMS ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: NO 4. ROUTE: MAN-LON-ROM-LON-MAN ELIGIBLE FOR FCOD: NO B Journey must be ticketed on BA 125 ticket stock C Ticketed fare must have “V2” or “V3” in the fare basis for the related fare component – “V2” indicates a PLUS fare and “V3” indicates a PLUS FLEX fare. Hotline fares "V2" or "V3" will show as "B2" or "B3" in the fare basis – (along with the "I" keywords below) D Change must be requested on the same calendar day as the scheduled departure of the original flight (based on UK date/time NOT the customer's local date/time at point of departure). E Change must be requested at least 1 hour prior to the originally scheduled departure time of the original flight. If checked in the customer needs to be offloaded from original flight F Requested change must be to an earlier or later flight between the same airport pair on the same calendar day, i.e. if booked LCY-BHD the airport cannot be changed to LHR-BHD. The routing must stay as LCY-BHD. G Requested change must be to another eligible flight. H Subject to availability in the same cabin. If bags have been checked in the customer cannot change on the day I The following keywords MUST be in the booking: PRDB BA HK1 FARES FAMILES – PLUS PRFB BA HK1 Or PRDC BA HK1 FARE FAMILES – PLUS FLEX PRFB BA HK1 J - The original booked flight must be one of the following: Marketed by: BA Operated by: BA Marketed by: BA Operated by: CJ (BA Cityflyer) Marketed by: BA Operated by: AO (BA EuroFlyer) Marketed by: BA Operated by: IB Marketed by: BA Operated by: Wetlease Further to this, the following T&Cs apply: Note reference i. Change must be requested on the same calendar day as the scheduled departure of the original flight (based on UK date/time NOT the customer's local date/time at point of departure). ii. Change must be requested at least 1 hour prior to the originally scheduled departure time of the original flight. If checked in the customer needs to be offloaded from original flight iii. Requested change must be to an earlier or later flight between the same airport pair on the same calendar day iv. Requested change must be to another eligible flight, see table above v. Subject to availability in the same cabin. If bags have been checked in the customer cannot change on the day How to check eligibility? To check FCOD eligibility you should look for the existence of either the PRDB or PRDC SK keywords which will be sector related to any eligible sectors. Alongside either of these keywords should be a PRFB SK keyword, which again will be sector related. These keywords will be automatically added to any eligible bookings which meet all the criteria i,ii,iii & iv above at point of sale.

question: What is the eligibility criteria for Proactive Uprade (POU)?
ground_truth: For bookings which have been through a Proactive Upgrade (POU) are still eligible providing the ticket prior to the upgrade meets the criteria. The fare basis on the ticket will have changed and the Fares Families keywords which indicate eligibility will have dropped out. In this situation, you should: - Check that the booking would have been eligible for FCOD prior to the POU – check the previous ticket for “V2” or “V3” ("B2" or "B3" for Hotline fares) in the fare basis and check the PNR history for SK keywords
context: Bookings with a Proactive Upgrade (POU) For bookings which have been through a Proactive Upgrade (POU) are still eligible providing the ticket prior to the upgrade meets the above criteria. If the original booking class is available on the new flight: 1.1. Amend the unwanted segment in the PNR to the required flight in same booking class 1.2. Select F10 > Option 2 – voluntary e-ticket change 1.3. The PNR will automatically update and the e-ticket will be revalidated 2. If the original booking class is not available on the new flight: 2.1. Amend the unwanted segment in the PNR to the required flight in the lowest booking class in the same cabin 2.2. Select F10 > Option 2 – voluntary e-ticket change 2.3. The PNR will automatically update to show the new flight details but in the original booking class and the e-ticket will be revalidated The routing (origin and destination airports) must remain unchanged. Routing or date changes made on the original date of departure may incur fare and/or tax differences, as usual. What to do if FCOD fails in Pegasus In the unlikely event the web service is down and customers wish to process a free change on the day, Pegasus will be unable to force book and users will see a red banner asking the customer to be referred to the airport. In this situation you should follow the airport process: 1. Reinstate the unwanted segment – you should now have the original segment in the original booking class AND the new segment in the highest booking class in the same cabin 2. If the original booking class is not available to rebook you should request for this to be reinstated via the Rev Man helpdesk 3. Queue the booking to LONBA07O9/50 4. Ignore and re-retrieve the PNR until the space is converted to the original class and the e-ticket revalidated If the free change is successful, there should be a new element: "SSR OTHS 1A FREE CHANGE SUCCESSFUL". If the rebooking is successful but ticket revalidation failed there should be a new element: "SSR OTHS 1A FREE CHANGE FAILED 12 – REVAL ERROR – PLS REVAL MANUALLY". In this case, manually revalidate the ticket. This does not apply to Open Jaw bookings. 2) Inform the passenger of the minimum fee (Our Service Fee - Add infant wherever applicable) and that a separate payment link will be sent from SL for ticket price for adding the infant according to the pricing.
4) Note down the full name and date of birth of the infant both in the Text to customer field in your Add on cart as well as in your errand.
5) Ask to which passenger the infant will be associated with and for which flights (whole, OB, IB, if multi) (please pay attention to the character limit, the adult with the shorter name would be the best option to select).
6) If the passenger pays over the phone, proceed with Register Errand, selecting the ‘'Ticketing template/ Tkt info add infant''.
7) Place on queue in Edvin in order to queue to ticketing ATH, UPA, BOM, CNX and WNS.

If so, check if invol refund/reissue guidelines is provided in the SC policy, or FL/SC agent need to contact YY for authorization of re-association after the reissue or full refund. For Gordian guide, please check here<>. 13) Identify the airline that owns the ticket (validating carrier) 14) Check Edvin Documents for SC policy of the specific airline Note : While handling SC and communicating with the customer, ETG policy will override YY policy in Edvin Document. However, to have e-ticket and itinerary aligned, please follow the Edvin document. 15) If the order is VI, then place the booking on VI SC Support queue in Edvin. 16) Handle the case through the Workmode<>. In the Common panel, specify the general information about the rule, such as its name, rule type and validity period. Note: The rule name does not have to be unique. In the Product panel, specify: – Information about the product to which this rule applies, such as the provider. – The type of product, such as Transportation. – Any sub-type, such as Air, Hotel, Ancillary, and so on. 4. If the conditions of more than one rule are met for a particular booking, the rule with the most matching criteria is applied. If, however, the competing rules have an equal number of criteria, then the rule with the highest weighting is selected. (Each rules weighting value is defined by the Margin Manager rule engine, and is not visible.) To specify that the rule applies to a particular market, you must select Any from the International indicator field, and Market from the Origin type or Destination type fields. question: What advantages does a Customer gain from having an ARN?
ground_truth: Found possible response for your query. Please refer to the document(s) below The advantages a Customer gains from having an ARN include being able to contact their bank and locate the funds using the transaction reference provided.
context: ARN guidelines: 1. *What is ARN? ARN stands for Acquirer Reference Number. It is the reference number given to a refund transaction when it is processed. This number can be used by the Customer/Bank to locate the refund processed at our end.##*Why do we provide ARN to a Customer? When a payout has been processed on our end, but the Customer has trouble locating the refund in their accounts, we provide them with the ARN in order to contact their bank and locate the funds using the transaction reference.##*What are the different terms for ARN on the different Payment Systems (PSP)? Note that all PSPs do not have the ARN option. Some payment systems have a direct connection with the Customer. Therefore, in such cases we are not able to provide ARN. The table below gives you a snapshot of which Payment systems have an ARN visible. For the detailed steps please follow the links for the respective PSPs. Payment System - Checkout Information - The ARN is always to be found on the platform Payment System - Yandex Information - The ARN is always to be found on the platform Payment System - Klarna Information - Klarna is invoices since the Customer has a direct connection with the Company . There is no ARN visible on the platformbecause there is none in general. Payment System - Ogone Information - ARN has to be requested by PSP - not visible in platform Payment System - Worldpay Information - Contract has been terminated. Payment System - Adyen Information - There are 5 different scenarios in Adyen. In some of themwe cannot retrieve ARN. 1. Adyen standard - The ARN is always to be found on the platform 2. Adyen V4 - The ARN is always to be found on the platform 3. Adyen with Klarna - The ARN is always to be found on the platform 4. Adyen external partner (Outsourcing) - ARN to be requested from PSP- not visible in platform 5. Adyen Trustly - ARN to be requested - the one visible does not help Customers locate refund with their bank

question: List of the most common claim types managed by the CR department
ground_truth: The most common claim types managed by the CR department include: 1) Ancillaries purchased by the customer but not added by ETG, resulting in the customer being forced to purchase them at the airport. 2) Ticketing issues/mishandling of reissue, where the customer requested a rebooking but it was not processed, leading to the customer buying a new ticket at the airport. 3) Schedule change mishandling, where customers claim refunds for costs incurred due to errors in schedule change handling. 4) Cancellation of tickets without customers' confirmation, resulting in extra costs for customers to reinstate the ticket or purchase new tickets.
context: Claims and complaints: 1. *List of most common claims -handled by CR department List of claims Please note the following examples cover the most frequent scenarios, not all. Customer requested and paid for rebooking but we did not proceed with the action resulting in the customer purchasing a new ticket at the airport. The customer has proof of the cost incurred. A flexible ticket service which could not be used, is NOT a claim, follow this link for more information. 3) Schedule change mishandling.Customer claiming refunds for costs incurred due to an error that may stem from our agency in regards to schedule change handling (e.g ticket was not reissued accordingly and due to that the customer had to buy a new ticket at the airport).Customer has proof of the cost incurred. 4) Cancellation of tickets without customers confirmation, resulting in extra cost for customers to reinstate the ticket directly with the airline or the need to purchase new tickets. question: How does a Schedule Change differ from a Force Majeure situation?
ground_truth: Found possible response for your query. Please refer to the document(s) below Schedule change is a general policy provided by the airline for involuntary handling scenarios, such as modification to the flight schedule before the departure date due to the airline's operational reasons, like change of time schedule, flight number, misconnection, additional stop, or airport change. On the other hand, Force Majeure is for unforeseeable circumstances that prevent the airline from operating the flight, such as epidemic/pandemic (COVID-19), damage to infrastructure due to an extraordinary situation (Blast in Beirut), natural disasters (Tsunami, Typhoon, Earthquake), strikes, bankruptcy, or air traffic congestion. Airlines provide exceptional policies and guidelines for Force Majeure scenarios based on certain criteria, such as travel date or route.
