question: What does Involuntary Reissue and Revalidation mean in the context of flight irregularities?
ground_truth: Found possible response for your query. Please refer to the document(s) below Involuntary reissue allows you to reissue a ticket without an extra cost or waiving a fee when there is an involuntary rerouting due to unplanned disruptions or planned schedule changes by the airline. Revalidation is a process in which whenever a change is done on the reservation, the ticket numbers remain the same, and the information on the itinerary needs to match with the ticket.
context: General Info for Flight Irregularities: 1. *Terminology 1) Involuntary Reissue / Revalidation 1.1) Accept the alternative means whenever a schedule change is done on the reservation the ticket numbers remain the same, and no need to get the tickets reissued/revalidated even if the time is not matching as long as the date, flight number and airports are the same. Customer can just present his original ticket at the airport for check in, even though your new itinerary is different with the ticket. Note that in this scenario the confirmation of the segments (ERK/EWR) is required. 1.2) Revalidation - Its a process in which whenever a change is done on the reservation the ticket numbers remain the same. The Informationrmation on the itinerary needs to match with the ticket. 1.3) Reissue means replacement of an existing air ticket with a new air ticket. Involuntary reissue allows you to reissue a ticket without an extra cost or waiving a fee, when there is an involuntary rerouting due to unplanned disruptions or planned schedule changes by the airline. Obviously reissuing a ticket is more time consuming and costly than revalidation, but not all date changes require reissue. 1.4) Re-Routing means a change in the origin, destination, transit, or stopovers originally ticketed. 2) Involuntary refund 2.1) Involuntary Refunds means a refund of an unused ticket or portion there of or an unused miscellaneous charges order required as a result of the carrier cancelling a flight, failing to operate a flight according to schedule, failing to stop at a point to which the passenger is destined or is ticketed to stop over, or causing the passenger to miss a connecting flight, being unable to provide previously confirmed space, substituting a different type of equipment or class of service or where, because of safety or legal requirements or the condition or conduct of the passenger, carriage is refused. An electronic ticket can be refunded either directly via the GDS in the office the ticket was issued or through BSPlink. 2.2) [GDS Global Distribution System, such as Amadeus, Sabre, or travelport. 2.3) [BSP Billing and Settlement Plan is an IATA electronic billing system to run and simplify the interchange of data and funds between travel agencies and airlines. Sounds complicated, but in plain English, BSP is a payment mediator between airlines and travel agents. 3) EMD An EMD (Electronic Miscellaneous Document) is an electronic voucher issued by an airline or designated agency. The EMD is of the value indicated on the front, and is issued as a coupon to be used for the purpose described thereon, or for handling fees. Usually the EMD issued for ancillaries via GDS systems, such as baggage, seats, etc. As EMD corresponds to a ticket customer can find it in the booking reference on his/her ticket or in the confirmation e-mail we have sent to them after completing their reservation. 4) Waiver: What is this? Travel waivers sometimes refer to situations in which an airline allows a passenger to waive travel because there are safety concerns. For example, a waiver allows customers to change their itinerary with no fare differences if they remain in the same cabin as originally booked, such kind of criteria can be found under Edvin Documents. Note that airline use different waivers for their policy or flows. For example airline can request to add an endorsment during cancellation or reissue, or add an OSI line before any actions, or add a Tour Code in a specific field. It is important to mention that different processes should be followed for each waiver, so FL agent need to provide clear instruction to SL agent of the action he/she needs to follow. 5) Inactive segments and non show Please keep in mind that there are some airline companies that require us to remove the inactive segments from the PNR, before the departure. The inactive segments usually have a status UN/UC/US/NO or HX. The Ticketing team is working on removing the inactive segments to avoid any financial costs for the company. What this means is that sometimes you might find PNRs without flight segments, specifically for orders with close departures. You will probably see the following in GDS as an indication of the above (but sometimes it will be a regular ghostline): MIS 1A HK1 STO 04MAR-SEGMENT REMOVED TO AVOID CHARGES All PNRs impacted by Covid19 with inactive segments (UN/HX/NO/UC) we will now handle as per the airlines FM guidelines in Travel Alert pages. One such segment in the order (not referring to Multiple PNRs) is enough to consider it affected and handle as per FM policy. This applies to all types of cases, refund/open ticket/voucher/rebookings. Handle the PNR accordingly, regardless of the original departure date. Furthermore, when we follow FM policy, if the airline has a deadline to fulfill a certain process (deadlines for rebookings etc.), this cannot be ignored even if we have a case with inactive segments. We have to stick to the process and follow the airlines guidelines. Please note that if the segments were active (HK) before the customer being marked as a no-show, we have to follow normally the no-show policy. Thus, you need to check the history of the PNR in GDS to be sure of how to proceed in each case. A ‘no show’ designation refers to a ticketed passenger that has failed to check in or board their booked flight. Some airlines used the definition NoShow even before departure which might restrict some actions like rebookings and cancellations. 6) Validating Carrier VS Interline VS Codeshare 6.1) Validating Carrier (VC) : The responsible owner for the ticket Example: JetBlue Only Reservation (B6/279 Ticket Stock) Example Itinerary: B6 79 01JAN JFKMCO 0600 B6 54 08JAN MCOJFK 0700 Example Ticket: 2791234567890 6.2) Interline is a relationship between airlines which allows one airline sells services to a customer that are provided by another airline. 6.2.a) Example: Interline Reservation (B6/279 Ticket Stock) Example Itinerary: B6 940 01JAN MCOBOS 0800 EI 136 01JAN BOSDUB 1815 Example Ticket: 279123456789 6.2.b) Interline Reservation (Airline Partner Ticket Stock) Example Itinerary EK 203 01JAN DXBJFK 0225 B6 31 01JAN JFKMCO 1040 Example Ticket: 1261234567890 6.3) Codeshares allow us to sell seats on flights operated by other airlines. This means you can easily combine American and flights with other partner airlines to create a single itinerary to multiple destinations. Example: Codeshare Reservation (B6/279 Ticket Stock) Example Itinerary B6 940 01JAN MCOBOS 0800 B6 5018 01JAN BOSDUB 2215 Example Ticket: 279123456789 7) Consolidator IATA accredited agency issuing tickets on behalf of non-IATA accredited agency 8) PNR A PNR, or Passenger Name Record, is basically a term meaning ‘reservation’. Airlines will often ask agents for a PNR locator, also known as their reservation, booking or confirmation number. Passenger Name Record is a code with 6 alphanumeric characters (letters and numbers are used together) 9) Ticket number First three digits identifies the airline (117- SAS, 125- British Airways, 074-KLM etc) followed by 10 numbers that is unique for that ticket. It is created once the payment is confirmed to the airline and the ticket is issued. It is mandatory for each customer to have this in order to travel 10) Glossary of most common abbreviation 10.1) ADM - Agency Debit Memo 10.2) EMD(-S) / EMD(-A) - Electronic Miscellaneous Document S = Standalone; A = Associated 10.3) Exchange - Change of unused tickets, where change includes the first flight coupon 10.4) FBA - Free baggage allowance 10.5) FOC - Free of Charge 10.6) Flight irregularity - A flight irregularity is any situation that prevents a passenger from travelling as 10.7) originally booked – where the passenger is not at fault 10.8) HX - Segment status code – holding cancelled (flight is operating) Lufthansa Group 10.9) Agency Support - Agency support for OS/LH/LX/SN documents 10.10) OAL - Other Airlines: all airlines except OS, LH, LX, SN, EW, 4Y, WK 10.11) Prime Flight - Flight operated and marketed by the same airline 10.12) RBD - Booking Class – Reservation Booking Designator 10.13) Reissue - In this policy: includes exchange (change of unused tickets, where change includes the first flight coupon) and reissue (change of partially flown tickets) 10.14) SC - Schedule Change (status code of the new flight segment), shown 10.15) SSR - Special Service Request 10.16) TK - Segment status code - Advise passenger new flight times 10.17) UN - Segment status code - Unable, does not operate 10.18) 1day - “One day” is defined by calendar day. The flight segment status is changed on the day of departure (= day 0) or the day before departure (= day -1) of the original flight E.g.: Original flight departure 18FEB Notification: 17FEB or 18FEB=>INVOL Notification: on/before 16FEB=>SKCHG

question: What is an External Portal (NDC) and how is it used during flight disruptions?
ground_truth: Found possible response for your query. Please refer to the document(s) below External Portal (NDC) is a direct connection with the airline for orders with a portal. During flight disruptions, the External Portal (NDC) is used to create a direct connection with the airline and to follow the airline policy for Full Service Carriers (FSC). Notifications about flight irregularities are received through the portal, and the information can be found under each portal's information.
context: General Info for Flight Irregularities: 1. *Flight Irregularities - Notification Systems GDS - Global Distribution System A global distribution system is a computerized network system owned or operated by a company that enables transactions between travel industry service providers, mainly airlines, and travel agencies. The GDS mainly uses real-time inventory from the service providers. ETG use Amadeus, Sabre and travelport as GDS. Since most of the airlines are FSC (Full service carrier) we handle all the schedule change notifications that occur more than 24 hours (or 48 hours), according to our contracts with airlines. Such Informationrmation can be displayed under Edvin Docs. Edvin Docs: Informationrmation about External portal SC handling can be found under: 1. Edvin Docs ⇾ Carrier ⇾ SC Information - Full Airline Name (2-letter code) 2. For each GDS system, we have a different file in Shelf: GDS << https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/?cp=1&fi=8966b3ef-901d-4ec7-9799-36f02888bd36&it=snippet&ps=50&sb=TITLE&sl=en&so=ASC >> Notifications: In GDS systems, airline sent us a notification about the change in Q7 under each office ID for each PNR. We have a specific script automation to gather all the Informationrmation in one place. For more Informationrmation about the automation, click here << https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/read/3892d155-71d3-4309-8df1-b93b868d2768?parentId=11d2c410-66d3-43ba-b688-2bfcac55d48a&view=snippet-view&trigger=title&searchEventId=01GPGAP03K5EM6M6X7EQ3ESG6X&source=shelf >> External Portal (NDC) For orders with a portal, we create a direct connection with airline. We usually follow airline policy for the FSC (Full service carrier). Such Informationrmation can be displayed under Edvin Docs. Edvin Docs: Informationrmation about External portal SC handling can be found under: 1. Edvin Docs ⇾ Carrier ⇾ Full Airline Name (2-letter code) ⇾ System - (2-letter code) 2. Informationrmation about External portal FM handling can be found under: 1. Edvin Docs ⇾ Carrier ⇾ Full Airline Name (2-letter code) ⇾ FM Full Airline Name (2-letter code) 3. Shelf page for Portals. << https://etraveligroup.shelf.io/?cp=1&fi=d21185ba-7f86-488b-b109-bf7519152265&it=snippet&ps=50&sb=TITLE&sl=en&so=ASC >> Notifications: We have a specific way of receiving the Informationrmation in a queue of the portal or in through an email. This Informationrmation can be found under each portal Informationrmation. LCC - Low-Cost Carrier For LCC orders, it is difficult to distinguish the terms “Schedule change” and “Force Majeure”. In both scenarios, we receive email notifications in OTRS and unless the airline clearly mentions that the irregularity has occurred due to FM events, we are unable to separate SC from FM. At the same time, through the email notifications, the airline lets us know the alternatives the passenger can select. question: What do you mean by Payment Link?
ground_truth: Found possible response for your query. Please refer to the document(s) below A payment link is a form of payment that allows the customer to fulfill the payment outside of the call interaction. The agent sets the time frame for which the payment link will be active and sends the secure payment link directly to the customer’s contact email. The agent does not handle any sensitive data, as all the card details are inserted by the customer directly into the secure payment link. Once the payment is fulfilled, the payment link ends up in the Support dashboard.
context: Manual - Offline Reservations: 1. *8.Payment Link - Client This is what the client will receive on their end, in the form of an email, once they receive your “payment link”. Once the client clicks on the “Click here” link he/she will get prompted to fill in their credit card and billing information. They will also see the final price and components of their reservation. Once they process the payment the file will land with the back-office team who will finalize it, meaning accounting/ticketing etc. ------------------------- Payment methods for post-sale services: 1. *What is a Payment Link and when to use? What is it? A payment link is a form of payment, which allows the customer to fulfill the payment outside of the call interaction. The agent sets the time frame for which the payment link will be active and sends the secure payment link directly to the customer’s contact email. The agent is not handling any sensitive data, all the card details are inserted by the customer directly to the secure payment link. Once the payment is fulfilled, the payment link ends up in the Support dashboard When to use? A payment link is not a preferred payment method and should not be used as a first option. It can be used for the below scenarios: 1. for requests received via phone interaction, where customer could not proceed with the payment on the spot 1.1. Due to errors during the payment flow 1.2. Due to customer’s decision (e.g. customer does not have the payment card handy, declines processing via MOTO) ATT: MOTO should always be suggested as the first payment option. Payment link can be alternatively sent only if the above conditions are met and there is sufficient availability and remaining time before the scheduled departure! 2. for requests received via email interaction, which you are allowed to handle via email as per standard routines 3. for all requests for LATAM market orders as MOTO is not supported for those markets 4. for request from AU and CA market if the customer can use only Maestro card (if any other card - refer to MOTO) 5. during calls when active monitoring is in place (such as Supervisor monitoring or other agent shadowing) 6. when the customer wants to think or discuss about it before proceeding to the payment. This way, a possible second contact for the same reason might be avoided. Please note, that whenever you offer a Payment link, you shall state in your errand the reason why you could not use MOTO (i.e: pax denied MOTO, MOTO not enabled etc.). If MOTO is not available on a particular order or the customer declines using MOTO, but still wishes to proceed with the payment on the spot and during the phone call, you should wait on the line until the payment is processed and handle the paid request accordingly. Otherwise, you have to inform the customer that the price and availability are not guaranteed. The last payment date/time shall be set as described below for each type of request: For rebooking cases, the last payment date/time for Payment link shall be set for 30 minutes (in exceptional cases, when you have sufficient availability and when passenger clearly asks for longer time, you may set the Payment link for maximum 1 hour). The deadline of last valid time for Payment Link should be 16:30 local time for both ATH/UPA. REMINDER: The reissue request must be placed on the respective queue at least 4 hours before the original departure and/or at least 6 hours before the new flight. Otherwise, changes are not possible. For ancillary cases, the last payment date/time for the Payment link can be set for maximum 48 hours from the moment of sending the link, as long as this time frame is not passing the 48 hour before the departure. For all other cases, the last payment date/time for a Payment link can be set for maximum 24 hours from the moment of sending the link, as long as this time frame is not passing the 48 hour before the departure. NOTE: If you handle an order with scheduled departure within the next 48h and the request requires additional payment, you should always proceed via MOTO Payment method. DO NOT send Payment Link for such cases, unless the case falls under scenarios where MOTO can not be supported. Schedule change requests shall be handled as per separate guidelines. For more detailed information check 4) Schedule change handling page in this decision tree.

question: What should be done after auto handling Schedule change (SC) Script
ground_truth: Found possible response for your query. Please refer to the document(s) below After auto handling a schedule change (SC) script, if the process fails on any automated step (e.g. the reissue or revalidation fails, or an error occurs), then the script will place the order on the Ticketing Q, and the Ticketing team will pick up the ticket and reissue it.
context: Schedule change GDS Automation -SC Script: 1. *SC Script Automation What is the SC script ? Etraveli group has an automation for schedule change notifications in GDS systems. This automation is called Touchless in Amadeus, PBA in Sabre and ICM in Galileo, and it handles the ‘minor’ schedule changes automatically. How does it work? Wherever a schedule change occurs, the airline always places the PNRs in a GDS queue (Q5 or Q6) under each office ID. The script gathers those notifications in one office ID and then, according to the settings we have set, either automatically handles the minor schedule changes or places them in another queue for manual handling. In order to automatically handle a SC case, we have set up the configurations (1) and added an airline table with policies (2). What configurations do we have? (1) The settings we currently use for automatically handling minor SC in all the GDSs are: 1. Airline should provide us with a valid alternative (UN,TK or TK) 2. There should be no misconnection between the flights (MCT) 3. The schedule change that occurred should be within 23.5 hours 4. The schedule change that occurred should not have a date change. Note: each GDS system has its own unique way of automatic handling. The settings we currently use for manual handling in all the GDSs are: 1. Airline has not provided a valid alternative (UN flights) 2. There is a misconnection between the flights (MCT) 3. The schedule change is more than 23.5 hours 4. There is a date change (Original trip: 6 August 22:00/- New time: 7 August 00:30) 5. There are VI and VI Bcom orders included What is an airline table with policies? (2) Each airline provides us with the policy we should follow for schedule changes. For example endorsement, OSI line, how we should reissue the ticket, etc. The airline table contains all this information for each system in one place, and should be manually updated every time we have a new policy from the airlines. Note, that some of the airlines might request from us to contact them for authorization for each case. Those airlines are excluded from the airline table. This means that the script will always place such PNRs into the manual handling queue. What if the script cannot handle a case automatically? The script handles a case according to the settings we have set up but if the process fails on any automated step (e.g. the reissue or revalidation fails, or an error occurs), then the script will place the order on the Ticketing Q, and the Ticketing team will pick up the ticket and reissue it. Note: According to our settings, it is possible to exclude an airline if, according to the policy of the carrier, we need to get an authorization before any action. In such cases, the script will never process the schedule change notification for those airlines and will always place it on manual queue for processing in accordance with the RM lines and our settings (for example VI orders or NZ airline - authorization required). What do the OSI/remark lines mean? Wherever the customer purchases an order on our website and the booking is created in the GDS, our system inserts some RM lines or OSI lines to identify the PNR market, locations or any kind of exceptions we need to have in order to handle this PNR. question: How do I request wheelchair assistance for a passenger?
ground_truth: To request wheelchair assistance for a passenger, you can use the following Amadeus entries based on the passenger's specific needs: - SRWCHR (ramp) for a passenger who can ascend/descend steps but requires a wheelchair for distance to/from the aircraft. - SRWCHS (steps) for a passenger who can walk but cannot ascend or descend stairs. - SRWCHC (cabin) for a passenger who is paraplegic/quadriplegic and requires an on-board wheelchair and assistance to/from the cabin seat. If more information is required by the airline, such as the reason for the request, it is recommended to include this information in the request. Additionally, passengers can bring their own wheelchair or walker free of charge, with specific requirements for dimensions and weight.

question: Passenger wants return refund due to illness after first flight using protection plan
ground_truth: Cancellation Protection Process - Medical Certificate The Cancellation Protection is valid for the following people in relation to one of the travelers: Close relative in this context means the insured party's husband, wife, children, grandchildren, siblings, parents, grandparents or parents-in-law, or a person that the insured party lives with as a couple as if they were married. The cancellation protection is valid for everyone in the order. For example, if friends are travelling and a parent of one of the travelers becomes ill and the certificate is approved by CR, this covers all people in the booking. The cancellation protection covers immediate illness or death only. If the customer has become ill after date of travel, this will not be approved. The illness has to prevent the traveler from travelling. Hence, if the traveler is visiting someone who has become ill and therefore does not want to go, this will not be approved as the traveler him/herself is not prevented from travelling (“purpose of travel no longer existing” as per the below-stated condition). If you feel that there are uncertainties when canceling, for example, the customer seems dishonest (states he or she is NOT ill but will still send a medical certificate either way), inform the customer that we consider insurance fraud to be a very serious take. Add any information in the booking for the evaluating department to see. Other dishonest situations may be that the customer is not able to obtain a visa for travel, booked incorrect dates, etc.

question: What exemptions apply to flex tickets
ground_truth: Flexible ticket If the product was purchased during the booking procedure, the Flexible Ticket allows you to change the date and/or time of your flight booking under the terms set out in this section. When providing our Flexible Ticket service, We only mediate the transport contract between You and the relevant airline. As the Flexible Ticket is our own service (i.e. You cannot make use of our Flexible Ticket service by contacting the airline directly) all rebooking requests making use of the Flexible Ticket service must be made via our customer service. Terms and conditions for Flexible Ticket The flexible ticket service allows rebooking of flights, subject to availability. If the amendment involves an upgrade to more expensive tickets, this shall be at the traveller's own expense. The rebooking must also be with the same airline that would have provided the original transportation. Changes made to a Flexible Ticket will only incur a penalty waiver. However, fare and tax differences will still apply. 1.Travelers cannot change the destination, either for the outbound or inbound journey. NOTE: If the customer makes a voluntary change in order to change the destination, the flexible product is no longer available for the new ticket. 2.Travelers cannot change the airport even within the same city. 3.The flexible ticket service does not permit name changes or name corrections. 4.The flights must be used in the order they were originally booked. 5.Upgrades to a different cabin on the same flight are not permitted. 6.Rebooking a ticket for a so-called stop-over is not permitted. 7.Travelers can only rebook the trip once and not per PNR. Once the change is confirmed, the rebooking service has been used and cannot be used again. 8.The flexible ticket can be used at least 24 hours before the original flight. See exception to this rule below.* If the outbound flight is flown, the product is still applicable until 24hrs before the original return flight. 9.In case of a multi PNR, if the customer requests to change the IB flight and the OB flight departs in less than the 24h, we can proceed with the change as the change reflects the PNR of the IB flight. 10.If the customer's type has changed, (child turning into an adult or an infant turning into a child) the traveler must pay the difference that occurred from the new type of code. 11.ETG is not responsible for information about visas if the trip is extended. 12.The new trip may not commence within 24 hours from the time of the change request. ATT: Due to the Covid-19 outbreak, exceptions may apply. For more details click HERE <> 12.When the rebooking is completed, ETG takes no responsibility for any supplementary services such as luggage and seat reservations that have been booked directly with the airline. Follow the rules of the new reissued ticket in case the ticket is exchanged due to flexible ticket and then customer requests cancellation. 13.If a passenger fails to appear for any section of the journey, the rebooking option is no longer valid. 14.The cancellation protection is not valid once the flexible ticket is used as it is connected to the first date of departure. 15.The cancellation guarantee is valid once the flexible ticket is used, even if a new order is created. 16.The flexible ticket service will not be refunded if the trip is cancelled, unless the 24h rule is applicable - see below. 17.If the passenger has a Flexible ticket and is cancelling against the 24h rule, and is eligible for refund, then ensure you run the Modify order by using the option "24h airline rule". Payout agents will refund the ticket and the flexible ticket product. 18.Always rebook the original ticket if possible according to fare rules, even if there is a high difference in price. No discount on high price difference! 19.If the original booking is a OWC or Multi PNR, and both tickets are "changes not permitted" according to the airline rule we still make two separate tickets as the original. 20.Flexible Ticket service is offered per person only to those with a physical seat (infants do not have seat) However, even though Infants do not hold a seat, they will still be included in the service if the adult that the infant is associated with, has purchased the Flexible Ticket. 21.The Flexible Ticket must be booked and paid for during the booking process and cannot be added afterwards NOTE: You can find here how to rebook the ticket via flexible ticket and any exceptions that may apply. 22. Please note that when re-issuance is not possible and a new ticket must be issued, we can offer a different airline to the customer as an exception if it is cheaper. This exception must be pointed out to the customer as the product rules state that rebooking is only with the same airline. Also, you should get the customer's confirmation before issuing a new ticket with a different airline. Search for the cheapest option using Amadeus Master Pricer, offer the customer the cheapest option (all airlines, but do not offer overnight alternatives). 23.In scenarios where we have not been able to provide the Flexible ticket service and we need to refund the extra amount paid (fare difference) or value of the ticket, it is very important that the information in the SL is very clear. We do NOT offer any kind of compensation to the customer if he proceeds with a change directly with the airline. 24.If we will be refunding the penalty or the value of the ticket, use modify order with reason ‘Failed Flex Rebooking’ and also include the connected ancillaries to the ticket (seat, bag). Also add a note as bellow: Please refund the pax change fee XXXXXX or ticket value XXXXXX. 25.If we will be refunding the extra cost paid by the passenger for the rebooking that was not processed successfully, use modify order with reason ‘Ancillary- Voluntary’. *Exception If a customer contacts us in less than 24 hours the following criteria must be met to proceed with the rebooking. - Changes are permitted according to fare rules (If we notice that the airline charge an additional No Show fee then this has to be paid by the customer*) * Examples related to the No Show fee -Many airlines have one fee for changes and a higher one for No show, and according to the fare rules in case of No show, we charge one, the highest. E.g. Changes: 60 EUR No show: 80 EUR Since the highest fee is the No Show fee ( 80 EUR), the amount of 80 EUR will be charged to the customer. -Many other airlines have one fee for changes and one fee for No show, and in case of No show, we charge both. E.g. Changes: 60 EUR No show: 60 EUR In this example, only the No show fee ( 60 EUR) will be charged to the customer, while the remaining 60 EUR (Change fee) will be covered and paid to the airline by us. -There are also other airlines that have one fee for changes and one lesser fee for No show, and in case of No show, we charge both. E.g. Changes: 60 EUR No show: 50 EUR In such cases only the No show fee (50 EUR) will be charged to the customer, while the remaining 60 EUR (Change fee) will be covered and paid to the airline by us. - We are able to rebook and reissue before departure (not in cases of changes not permitted on original ticket) - The new trip may not commence within 24 hours from the time of the change request. Let the customer know this is an exception from our travel terms and condition. No show -If it is possible as per fare rules to rebook after no show, offer this alternative to the customer with all applicable fees. Same with destination changes/open jaws and stopovers – offer this to the customer as per fare rules if possible with all applicable fees. -If the customer chooses to rebook paying all applicable fees due to no-show/destination changes/open jaws/stopover, Flexible Ticket is still valid and can be used later within original terms and conditions. Cancellation A ticket that has been rebooked using the Flexible Ticket is non-refundable to the customer in case of cancellation, regardless of the ticket fare rules. A ticket that has been rebooked using the Flexible Ticket will be refunded according to the standard refund process of voluntary reissued tickets. This means that we need to check the rules of both the original ticket and the new ticket to determine which penalty to charge for the refund. For more information check here. Tax refund, Force Majeure and Schedule Change as exceptions, see below:. Tax Refund Passengers always have the right to claim their taxes on the tickets. If a passenger wants their taxes, send for a tax refund, minus our refund fee, as a normal booking Force Majeure/Schedule Change If the new flights are affected by the schedule change or Force Majeure situation, and the customer received authorization for a full refund from the airline or it is clear that the new ticket is eligible for a full refund; we will provide it, less our refund fee, but as per the original ticket/order value. Possible customer for manual sales This product is NOT to be offered after purchasing the order in any case. Also the customer cannot purchase the product via Manage my booking. FAQ Question Where do I find the price for the product? Answer The product is not to be sold post booking any more. It has been removed from the add on cart on Edvin. Question Can I offer Flexible ticket to a customer that did their booking more than one day ago? Answer No. The product should only be purchased during the booking process. Question Should I offer to add the Flexible ticket to a customer who call us within the correct time limit and asking to rebook their ticket Answer No. The product should only be purchased during the booking process. Question What if they booked in the morning the day before and calls us in the afternoon the day after, can I still offer the products? Answer No. The product should only be purchased during the booking process. Question Can I offer the product to all customers in all markets? Answer No. The product should only be purchased during the booking process. Question Can I add the product to just one of the persons in the booking? Answer No. The product should only be purchased during the booking process.

question: How to invoke CFAR for booking cancellation
ground_truth: Step by Step - Cancel with waiver in fare rules Cancel with waiver in fare rules - Amadeus 1. Open PNR in respective office id, use RT+PNR 2. Check Ticket status (O or A) in ticket line. Use RTTN to open ticket line. TWD/L1 to open ticket. 3. Check fare rules and/or Edvin CXL docs if the waiver is valid. If yes we proceed with the below. 4. Confirm cancellation of segments with the customer to avoid no show. 5. If split of passengers is required, do not split in GDS, proceed with next step. 6. When sending to refund; use Modify Order in Edvin and choose cancellation reason GDPR waiver. Choose the passenger who confirmed cancellation.Register errand with all fees in detail ( check our fee in Edvin if applicable). Do not mention the reason, just cxl with yy gdpr waiver fare rule/edvin cxl med docs. 7. Send cancellation confirmation email from Edvin. Choose a template relevant to the reason of the waiver - ‘’CXL conf – med cert waiver'’, CXL conf - death cert waiver or CXL conf - visa rejection cert waiver. Passenger has to upload the documents only via the link in the confirmation.
